pinyin: fèng tiān chéng yùn，huáng dì zhào yuē
literal: receive · heaven · carry · mandate · emperor · decree · say
natural: by the mandate of Heaven, the Emperor decrees

meaning.en: The opening formula of Ming and Qing imperial edicts; today used jokingly to announce an order or decision.
meaning.zh: 明清两代圣旨开头的套语；今天常戏用于宣布命令或决定。

examples.zh: 他清了清嗓子：“奉天承运，皇帝诏曰——今晚火锅我请！”
examples.en: He cleared his throat: 'By the mandate of Heaven, the Emperor decrees — hotpot tonight is on me!'

examples.zh: 电视剧里，太监一开口就是“奉天承运，皇帝诏曰”。
examples.en: In the TV drama, the eunuch begins every edict with 'By the mandate of Heaven, the Emperor decrees'.

usage.en: Introduced under the first Ming emperor and kept by the Qing; best known today from costume dramas. Usually followed by the edict and closed with 钦此. Used playfully.
usage.zh: 明初开始使用，清代沿用；今天多因古装剧而为人熟知。后面接诏书内容，以“钦此”结尾。多为戏用。

natural: lord of nine thousand nine hundred years

meaning.en: The flattering title given to the late-Ming eunuch Wei Zhongxian, one step below the emperor's 万岁; used of a powerful figure who wields power behind the throne.
meaning.zh: 明末宦官魏忠贤的谄媚称号，仅次于皇帝的“万岁”；比喻权势熏天、仅次于最高统治者的人。

examples.zh: 他在公司里俨然成了九千九百岁，连老板都让他三分。
examples.en: He has become the power behind the throne at the company; even the boss defers to him.

examples.zh: 魏忠贤被称为九千九百岁，各地还为他修建生祠。
examples.en: Wei Zhongxian was hailed as 'Lord of Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Years', and shrines were built to him across the empire.

usage.en: Sarcastic when applied to a modern person. Often shortened in speech to 九千岁, the more common form of the title.
usage.zh: 用于今人时带讽刺意味。口语里也常说“九千岁”。
